standard.title: Features of spoken language for fluency
standard.description: demonstrate how features and conventions of spoken Chinese can extend fluency when responding to and creating texts appropriate to contexts, purposes and audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can examine phonological features, monitor pronunciation against standard models, and perform target language texts (AC9LCH8EU01). They have compared own speech with standard forms. They have not yet applied spoken language features to extend fluency in debate and argument contexts, prepared formal speeches for real audiences, or analysed rap, comedy and performance forms for phonological technique.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students demonstrate how features and conventions of spoken target language extend fluency — including comprehension of diverse accents, performance techniques, and formal speech delivery for real audiences.

nodes.label: Comprehension and discrimination across accents and speeds
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop strategies for understanding unfamiliar voices at varied speeds and discriminating between unfamiliar homophones and regional variation.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate comprehension of at least two spoken texts from unfamiliar voices or speeds, identify at least two unfamiliar homophone pairs, and describe at least one strategy used for each.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to interactions between unfamiliar voices at varied speeds; apply comprehension strategies; discriminate between unfamiliar homophones; enhance fluency through rap songs or stand-up comedy; identify regional variation in pronunciation across Chinese-speaking environments.
wider: Research a specific regional variety of the target language — describe the phonological features, find examples, and explain the comprehension strategies most useful for that variety
Compare comprehension strategies across multiple regional accents encountered — identify which strategies transfer and which are variety-specific
nodes.hinge_reason: Comprehension across diverse speakers and speeds is the prerequisite for authentic spoken language use at Y9-10. Students who can only understand familiar speakers or slow, teacher-directed speech cannot function in real-world target language listening contexts.

response_modes.reason: Acoustic comprehension across diverse speakers is built through varied, repeated listening exposure. Systematic encounter with different voices, speeds, accents and registers builds the flexible processing capacity needed.

success_criteria: Demonstrates comprehension of at least two spoken texts from unfamiliar voices or speeds
Identifies at least two homophone pairs and describes a strategy for discrimination

nodes.label: Performance techniques for rhythm and fluency
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with rhythm, pace, tone and stress in performance contexts — rap, comedy, poetry, drama — and develop strategies to enhance communication for specific audiences.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one performance demonstrating deliberate use of at least two prosodic features (rhythm, pace, tone variation, stress) for communicative or artistic effect.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with rhythm, pace, tone and stress; take on the role of a news reader or performer; practise rap or stand-up comedy in the target language; read poems in multiple ways to convey different meanings; watch and perform versions of target language cultural performances.
wider: Create an original performance text — rap, spoken word, or monologue — demonstrating deliberate prosodic design choices, with annotation explaining each choice
Compare the prosodic techniques used in target language and English performance genres — identify what is shared and what is culturally specific to each

response_modes.reason: Performance technique requires practice across varied performance forms. Students who have only practised in one format — only poetry, or only formal speech — cannot generalise their prosodic skills. Varied performance contexts build flexible prosodic production capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students may have exposure to target language performance traditions — songs, poetry, comedy — from home or community. Width investment here connects these cultural resources to formal prosodic analysis, building genuine performance capability.
success_criteria: Produces a performance demonstrating deliberate use of at least two prosodic features
Can explain the intended communicative or artistic effect of each prosodic choice

nodes.label: Formal speech delivery for real audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliver formal speeches to real or realistic audiences using appropriate intonation, stress and phrasing — including debate presentations, welcome speeches, and argumentative oral texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a formal speech of at least two minutes using appropriate prosodic conventions, with at least one deliberate prosodic choice explained in terms of audience effect.
nodes.typical_width: Present arguments in debate using emphasis and persuasion; deliver formal speeches with focus on fluency and audience; present oral texts appropriate to formal contexts; use dictionaries and digital tools to support pronunciation; quote literary texts with appropriate intonation.
wider: Record and systematically review a formal speech delivery — identify specific prosodic choices and evaluate their effectiveness for the audience and purpose
Compare formal speech conventions in the target language with English debate or presentation norms — identify differences in pacing, pause conventions, and rhetorical delivery

response_modes.reason: Formal speech delivery integrates comprehension strategy awareness (node 1) and performance technique (node 2) into a full formal spoken production task. The teaching investment is in creating genuine formal audience conditions — real debates, real presentations — where prosodic control serves communicative purpose.

success_criteria: Delivers a formal speech of at least two minutes with appropriate prosodic conventions
Can identify and explain at least one deliberate prosodic choice made during delivery
